clue.text: See 19 across
Louis XIV's lost his crown? Annul his coronation!

definitions.meaning: a French monarch deprived of his throne has been dethroned, the clue's question mark flagging a descriptive reading
to undo a crowning is to strip a ruler of royal rank, a verb sense

explanation.surface: A history quiz asks what happened to the Sun King's crown and demands his coronation be cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a monarch is to strip him of kingship, which is what both halves describe.

clue.text: See 12
Bird brains following idol

indicators.note: following places the word for brains after the word for idol

parts.note: an idol is a worshipped god
brains, as in intelligence, means wit

explanation.surface: Someone with bird brains is chasing after a pop idol.
explanation.definitionFit: A godwit is a long-billed wading bird of marshes and estuaries.

clue.text: One star icon represented city

parts.note: one is the article a
the sun is our nearest star

indicators.note: represented signals that the letters of icon are presented again in a new order

explanation.surface: A single celebrity icon is portrayed as standing for a whole city.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunción is the capital city of Paraguay.

clue.text: See 24
Food covered in brown salt

indicators.note: covered in signals that one word is wrapped inside another

parts.note: to sear meat is to brown it
fare is food served

explanation.surface: A recipe direction: food is browned and covered in salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' looks like a seasoning in the recipe, but an old salt is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is an experienced sailor, a seafaring person.

clue.text: Figure one had nothing left

parts.note: one had is contracted to I'd, written as two letters
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone describes a person who once had a fortune and is left with nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a figure, a statue or image that is worshipped.

clue.text: Bitter, drunk sour, binds one, I say

indicators.note: binds signals the jumbled word wraps round the other pieces
drunk suggests the letters of sour are staggered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
one is the article an
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like I say

explanation.surface: Someone bitter after a sour drink is bound up in himself, he says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' turns SOUR into ROUS, which 'binds' AN plus COR to give R-ANCOR-OUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancorous describes deep, lasting bitterness or resentment.

clue.text: Bear — in cave? No, other way round

definitions.meaning: to bear fruit or crops is to produce them

definitions.text: in cave? No, other way round
definitions.meaning: turning the two words round gives cave in, which means to give way or submit

explanation.surface: A bear is found in a cave, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition tells you to swap the words, making the phrase 'cave in'.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is both to produce, as a field bears a crop, and to give way under pressure.

clue.text: See 22 down
Song of praise in 13 down makes wicked, cold Frank (witch) dash

parts.note: wicked is slang for excellent or marvellous
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
frank means candid or open
a hag is an ugly old witch
an en is a short printer's dash

explanation.surface: A song in a film tells how a wicked witch called Frank makes a cold dash.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 down is MOVIE: the song comes from the film Hans Christian Andersen and praises the Danish capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This song from a film musical praises the city of Copenhagen as marvellous.

clue.text: Stein's latest picture taken for the record

parts.note: a stein is a beer mug, and the 's stands for is
the latest news or fashion is hot

explanation.surface: Stein's newest photograph has been taken for the archive.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the start as 'mug's hot': a stein is a mug and the latest thing is hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A mugshot is a police photograph taken for official records.

clue.text: Picture of innocence's debut, wearing shift

indicators.note: wearing signals one piece goes inside another, like a body inside clothes

parts.note: to shift is to move

indicators.note: debut means the first appearance, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A portrait of innocence making its first appearance in a loose dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a dress, but it is the verb move.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is an informal word for a film, a movie.

clue.text: See 26
Not the only one to hold up a person who's late

definitions.text: Not the only one to hold up a person who's late

parts.words: Not the only one to hold up a person who's late
parts.note: reads like a robbery or delay, but a late person is a dead one and several carriers hold up the coffin

explanation.surface: Someone is not alone in delaying a latecomer.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffin carriers at a funeral share the task of shouldering the deceased.

clue.text: See 28
On the way out, not dead but very competitive

indicators.note: D for dead is swapped for V for very, as the words not and but direct

parts.note: on the way out means about to die

explanation.surface: Someone close to the end but not finished yet is very competitive.
explanation.definitionFit: Vying means competing, so it can stand for competitive.

clue.text: See 19
Mother ending in ruin (gin?) — "One way to catch a bloke"

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: ending in signals that only the final letter is taken

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: A mother's gin habit ends in ruin, and she jokes about catching a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' is not the drink but a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantrap is a device for catching trespassers, and also a seductive woman.

clue.text: Jazzman's hit, "Kind of Blue", popular with Maureen, old Bob and Daisy?

parts.note: midnight blue is a shade of blue
in means fashionable or popular
Mo is a short form of Maureen
a bob was a shilling, abbreviated s in old British money
Daisy is a traditional name for a cow, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A jazz musician's famous album, with a cast of friends called Maureen, Bob and Daisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of Blue' looks like the Miles Davis album; the hit is Kenny Ball's.
explanation.definitionFit: This tune was a 1960s chart hit for British jazz trumpeter Kenny Ball.

clue.text: Great energy-releasing round movement

indicators.note: releasing signals that the letter for energy is let go

parts.note: great means large
E is the physics symbol for energy
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A great release of energy causes a circular motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A largo is a slow movement in a piece of music.

clue.text: King Edward was exploitative, in the royal habit

parts.note: ER is Edwardus Rex, King Edward
mined, as in exploited resources

explanation.surface: A king was greedy in his regal dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' means clothing: ermine fur trims royal robes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermined means wearing ermine, the white fur of royal and noble robes.

clue.text: In which volume may/may not be turned up?

definitions.text: In which volume may/may not be turned up?

parts.words: In which volume may/may not be turned up?
parts.note: reads like a question about sound levels, but a volume is a book that may or may not be found on the shelves

explanation.surface: A question about where the sound may or may not be turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A place full of books is where a sought volume may or may not be found.

clue.text: Regent's Park Zoo lions and rockery plant?

definitions.meaning: a saxifrage grown in rock gardens

explanation.surface: Lions at the zoo and a plant in the rock garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Regent's Park is in the capital; London Zoo is located there.
explanation.definitionFit: London pride is a saxifrage, also apt for the capital's lions.

clue.text: Wear one item of underwear by day with elastic top

parts.note: one is the article a
a bra is an item of underwear

indicators.note: top signals the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Wear one item of underwear by day, with an elastic top.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to wear away by rubbing.

clue.text: Labour would be after this on stage — it's "New"!

indicators.note: new signals that the letters are made new by reordering

parts.note: it with the 's taken as is, a link

explanation.surface: Labour politics would be after this new stage, it says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' is the political party, but means childbirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestation is pregnancy, the period before giving birth.

clue.text: Memory of concert followed by talk of something to eat

indicators.note: followed by places the second piece after the first

parts.note: a gig is a concert

indicators.note: talk of signals a word said aloud

parts.note: a bite is something to eat

explanation.surface: Memory of a concert followed by talk of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigabyte is a unit of computer memory.

clue.text: Sporty type, unmanned, becomes "creative"

indicators.note: unmanned signals that the male pronoun is removed

parts.note: a hearty is a sporty, outdoor type

explanation.surface: A sporty type, without a man, becomes creative.
explanation.walkthrough: A HEARTY is British slang for a sporty extrovert; HE is a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty means artistic, creative.

clue.text: Avril's little pair in distress — aspirin dished out

indicators.note: in distress signals letters thrown into disorder

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for little

indicators.note: dished out signals letters handed round in a new order

explanation.surface: Avril's little pair is in distress, and aspirin is handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: Avril is French for April; 'pair in distress' and 'aspirin dished out' are anagrams.
explanation.definitionFit: Avril is the French word for April, so it is April in Paris.

clue.text: Colour of gunge after sulphur removed

parts.note: gunge is slime
S is the symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Colour of gunge after sulphur removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale yellowish-green shade named after the citrus fruit, so an example of a colour.

clue.text: Spirited account of grand entertainer on the level in US

parts.note: G is a grand
a host entertains
story is the US spelling of storey

explanation.surface: An account of a grand entertainer on the level in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghost story is a tale of spirits.

clue.text: Do housework, mother — it has great potential power behind it in America

definitions.text: it has great potential power behind it in America

parts.note: to hoover is to vacuum
a dam is a mother animal

explanation.surface: Do housework, mother, it has power behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoover Dam is a US hydroelectric dam.
